buildSourceNote: Build 138 carries v1.1.0-rc.14. The owner reported that the developer login 'needs every access'. The premise was wrong, and checking it found two real defects. The signed-in tab was sayeed_dp (user 21, gm_service), NOT the developer login - the only ACTIVE developer account is wmsdmworkshop@gmail.com (user 48); the older 'developer' account (user 30) is deactivated. Both the GM and the developer are named Sayeed, which is how the two get confused; the loaded account was confirmed by reading dwip_auth_user from localStorage rather than assuming. DEFECT 1: access is decided by three layers that can disagree - the API (AuthorizationService.checkPermission short-circuits admin and developer before any lookup, so developer genuinely may call any route), the tab-permission filter (isTabPermitted returns true immediately for developer), and the sidebar (ROLE_TABS, then the rc1 profile filter). rc1 is exactly what deployment/Dockerfile builds (VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE=rc1), and its excludedTabs list was written out TWICE with different behaviour: the redirect guard exempted admin, developer, dealer_principal, gm_service and workshop_manager while the sidebar filter exempted nobody. A privileged user could therefore deep-link to a screen the nav never offered, and developer - the widest ROLE_TABS in the file plus a full API override - silently lost six tabs in production with no way to tell why. The clearest evidence the filter was over-broad: the ROLE_TABS loop explicitly splices a Breakdowns tab in for developer and the managers, and the filter then deleted it again. Both call sites now share RC1_EXCLUDED_TABS and RC1_TAB_EXEMPT_ROLES through isRc1TabHidden(), so the two cannot diverge again; emptying RC1_TAB_EXEMPT_ROLES restores the old behaviour in one place instead of two. DEFECT 2, AND THIS ONE WAS MINE: rc.13 added 'reception' to GATE_OUT_SECURITY_ROLES but gave reception no way to use it. The only caller of POST /api/gate-out/gate-out in the entire repository is SecurityWorkspace.tsx:63, which renders only on activeTab === security-workspace, and ROLE_TABS.reception held just vehicle-lookup and gate-entry. MyWorkspace.tsx has ZERO gate or security references, so there was no fallback path either. Reception held the authority and had nowhere to use it. security-workspace is now in reception's list - added to reception ONLY, not receptionist, because granting the tab to a role the API does not authorise creates the inverse defect, a button that 403s; and security-workspace is absent from TAB_MODULE_MAPPING, so isTabPermitted passes it through. Also recorded while checking: security_agent and gate_personnel do NOT have that tab either - only admin, developer, workshop_manager, service_manager, gm_service and dealer_principal do - so gate-out has in practice been worked by admin and the GM, not by security. NOT CHANGED and flagged for the owner: service_manager, supervisor and floor_supervisor also have breakdown spliced in by the ROLE_TABS loop and are not in RC1_TAB_EXEMPT_ROLES, so they still lose it in production; widening that list is a policy decision about who sees Breakdowns in production. See docs/CHANGELOG.md.
